To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stator natural current and torque fluctuations of the DFIG system under the second grid faults may be influenced by those of the first grid faults, which may be used to predict the transient current and torque fluctuations during the first fault.

the DFIG wind system with rotor-side crowbar can ride through recurring symmetrical grid fault, but the transient rotor and the stator current and the torque fluctuations under the subsequent grid fault may be affected by the characteristic of preceding grid fault, and the stator natural current produced by voltage recovery after the preceding grid fault may be added to the stator natural component produced by the subsequent grid fault.

the stator and rotor currents and torque fluctuations under recurring grid faults are influenced by the characteristic (the voltage dips level and grid fault angle) of the first grid faults, as well as by the duration between two grid faults.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the characteristic of the previous grid fault on the DFIG performance during the second grid fault.
the influence of recurring grid faults on the DFIG performance and the corresponding control strategy, which will be useful in improving the DFIG wind turbines to meet the new grid code requirements.
the influence of the stator natural-flux superposition on the transient rotor and the stator current and the torque fluctuations under recurring symmetrical faults.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transient rotor current and torque fluctuations are not affected by the characteristic of recurring symmetrical grid fault, while the transient stator current and stator natural flux are influenced by the characteristic.

the stator and rotor current and torque fluctuations are affected by the characteristic of previous grid faults, which may lead to the deterioration of the wind turbine system performance and even the system instability.
the DFIG wind turbines with rotor side crowbar are able to ride-through recurring grid faults with the typical grid fault angles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the DFIG can ride through recurring symmetrical grid fault with a low-voltage ride- through strategy-with rotor-side Crowbar, and the transient rotor and the stator current and the transient rotor torque fluctuations under the first and the second grid fault are influenced by the characteristic and the duration between two grid faults.

the DFIG system is not suitable for the grid with recurring symmetrical faults, and the rotor-side crowbar is not effective in improving the performance of the DFIG system under recurring symmetri cal grid faults, which is different from the performance of the synchronous generator system under the same conditions.
the stator natural and the rotor induced fluxes should be taken into consideration in order to analyze the DFIG performance under recurring symmetrical faults.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transient performance of the DFIG system under recurring symmetri-cal grid faults is affected by the characteristic of preceding grid faults.
the DFIG can ride through recurring grid fault, and the transient rotor and torque fluctuation of the DFIG is affected by the characteristic of recurring grid faults.
the DFIG wind turbines should be equipped with the rotor current control strategy to suppress the stator current fluctuation and the rotor current fluctuation under recurring symmetrical faults.
